scope: Primary-paper and author-code inspection for complementary closed-geometry mechanochemical models; no replacement selected or implemented.
ranking: Reviewer judgment for the next implementation inspection, balancing mechanochemical polarity, real closed mechanics and practical source availability; not an exhaustive systematic review.
main_conclusion: No inspected candidate preserves the complete deBelly Rac/Rho–MCA–tension feedback while also supplying demonstrated uncut deforming mechanics. The strongest ready-code complementary candidate is Ivšić2026; the active-surface family supplies geometric mechanics; Werner2022 supplies explicit MCA/bleb closure.
important_distinctions: Minimal Model of Cellular Symmetry Breaking is PRL123188101(2019), not the separate PNAS11629–34(2019) paper.
A periodic computational box is distinct from a closed cell interface; Ivšić2026 has both. Bois2011 has only intrinsic periodic mechanics.
Axisymmetric meridional curves represent closed 3D surfaces and have pole regularity conditions; they are not periodic planar perimeter curves.
Substrate adhesion linkers in Chen2023/Shao2012 are not membrane-to-cortex attachments.
Published normal protrusion laws could motivate a new deBelly extension, but do not validate teleporting cut controllers or adding a tangential force without a transport closure.

candidates.label: Ivšić et al. (2026): GTPase-like chemistry, closed shape and hydrodynamics
candidates.title: Diversity in emergent cell locomotion from the coupling cytosolic and cortical Marangoni flows with reaction–diffusion dynamics
candidates.authors: Blaž Ivšić; Dorijan Vulić; Igor Weber; Piotr Nowakowski; Ana-Sunčana Smith
candidates.geometry: Actual deforming closed planar contour represented by a diffuse level set; the surrounding computational box is periodic.
candidates.mechanics: Incompressible low-Reynolds flow, activator-dependent normal protrusive force, curvature force, tangential Marangoni stress and drag.
candidates.biology: Four species represent a GTPase-like activation/inhibition cycle. Neither separate Rac/Rho antagonism nor MCA linkers is retained.
candidates.conservation: Mass-conserving reactions and confining potentials. Source-code stoichiometry conserves substrate+activator+complex and inhibitor+complex; their sum is not a count of four independent species.
candidates.cap_handling: No cap is removed: protrusion deforms the interface normally and species remain in the bulk/interface system.
candidates.feasibility: Public C implementation with example inputs; already a two-dimensional closed-cell model. Numerical conservation and mesh/time convergence still need independent checks.
candidates.use: Strongest implementation candidate for a complementary mechanochemical polarity model; adding deBelly MCA/Rac–Rho feedback would be new research.

candidates.label: Mietke and colleagues (2019–2026): closed active-surface mechanics
candidates.title: Minimal Model of Cellular Symmetry Breaking
candidates.authors: Alexander Mietke; V. Jemseena; K. Vijay Kumar; Ivo F. Sbalzarini; Frank Jülicher
candidates.geometry: Closed curved surface enclosing a viscous fluid. PRL nonlinear pattern simulations emphasize a rigid sphere; companion work evolves closed axisymmetric surfaces.
candidates.mechanics: Tangential and normal force balances, surface viscosity, active tension and bending; PRL couples to enclosed Stokes flow.
candidates.biology: Generic diffusing stress regulator; no Rac/Rho pair or explicit membrane–cortex attachment layer.
candidates.conservation: PRL includes surface advection, diffusion, geometric dilution and exchange with a dynamically updated well-mixed bulk pool.
candidates.cap_handling: No protruding cap is deleted. Normal motion and regularity at closed-surface poles replace nonzero tangential pole commands.
candidates.feasibility: 2026 public MATLAB code evolves closed axisymmetric surfaces. A meridian has pole conditions, not periodic planar-loop conditions; a planar reduction needs derivation.
candidates.use: Best source for a mechanically consistent normal-geometry extension. It supplies a framework, not an unchanged deBelly replacement.

candidates.label: Werner et al. (2022): explicit membrane–cortex linkers and blebs
candidates.title: A Diffuse Interface Model for Cell Blebbing Including Membrane-Cortex Coupling with Linker Dynamics
candidates.authors: Philipp Werner; Martin Burger; Florian Frank; Harald Garcke
candidates.geometry: Two closed diffuse interfaces represent membrane and cortex in a three-dimensional fluid domain.
candidates.mechanics: Fluid–structure interaction from membrane/cortex bending and surface energies plus nonlocal spring-linker coupling.
candidates.biology: Closest explicit MCA analogue: active/inactive linkers rip and repair according to membrane–cortex separation. No Rac/Rho signaling.
candidates.conservation: Opposite linker reaction terms conserve active+inactive linker number; general surface equations include advection and geometric dilution.
candidates.cap_handling: Bleb formation is normal separation of membrane from cortex; material stays represented rather than disappearing through a cap.
candidates.feasibility: Important limitation: all reported simulations freeze cortex and drop linker transport. A planar two-loop reduction and dynamic cortex need implementation.
candidates.use: Strongest source for MCA/normal-deformation closure; not a demonstrated self-polarizing model or immediate replacement.

candidates.label: Chen et al. (2023): normal protrusion on a deforming closed curve
candidates.title: Interplay Between Mechanosensitive Adhesions and Membrane Tension Regulates Cell Motility
candidates.authors: Yuzhu Chen; David Saintillan; Padmini Rangamani
candidates.geometry: Actual closed one-dimensional cell boundary evolving in a two-dimensional plane, initially near circular.
candidates.mechanics: Normal edge speed equals polymerization minus retrograde flow. Local adhesion/contractility/tension force balance and area-dependent, spatially uniform membrane tension close motion.
candidates.biology: Force-sensitive substrate adhesion fraction; no Rac/Rho chemistry. These extracellular adhesions are not MCA linkers.
candidates.conservation: Binding/unbinding evolves a local bound fraction with diffusion, rather than conserving an advected finite MCA pool.
candidates.cap_handling: The whole boundary moves continuously along its local normal. No cut, cap loss or endpoint controller.
candidates.feasibility: Closest economical closed-curve mechanical template. Equal-arclength remeshing is explicit; public implementation not located in inspected sources.
candidates.use: Useful alternative mechanical feedback model; adopting its uniform tension and substrate clutch substantially changes deBelly biology.

candidates.label: Shao et al. (2012): polymerization, viscous actin, adhesion and closed shape
candidates.title: Coupling actin flow, adhesion, and morphology in a computational cell motility model
candidates.authors: Danying Shao; Herbert Levine; Wouter-Jan Rappel
candidates.geometry: Closed moving planar cell boundary represented by a phase field; reported computations exploit mirror symmetry.
candidates.mechanics: Quasistatic viscous actin force balance includes expansive polymerization stress, myosin contraction, membrane tension/bending and gripping/slipping substrate adhesions.
candidates.biology: Actin and myosin fields; no explicit Rac/Rho pair or MCA. A polarized actin initial condition selects the front.
candidates.conservation: Actin monomer+filament conversion and myosin transport conserve their respective pools with zero-flux cell boundaries. Adhesion sites are replaced to keep their number fixed.
candidates.cap_handling: Protrusion emerges through distributed active stress and interface motion; no deleted cap.
candidates.feasibility: Already a two-dimensional closed-cell calculation, but full bulk mechanics is costlier than a perimeter-only assay.
candidates.use: Direct precedent for distributed polymerization stress; chemistry, adhesions and initialization prevent unchanged substitution for deBelly.

candidates.label: Bois et al. (2011): minimal consistent mechanics on a periodic domain
candidates.title: Pattern Formation in Active Fluids
candidates.authors: Justin S. Bois; Frank Jülicher; Stephan W. Grill
candidates.geometry: Fixed one-dimensional periodic thin-film domain: mechanical velocity and chemical concentration are both periodic.
candidates.mechanics: Viscous plus concentration-dependent active stress balances friction. The resulting flow advects the stress regulator.
candidates.biology: Generic conserved stress regulator, with extensions to reacting species; no Rac/Rho pair, separate membrane or MCA.
candidates.conservation: The single-species example uses conservative diffusion–advection and conserves its spatial integral.
candidates.cap_handling: No protrusion or normal shape dynamics. A periodic coordinate closes intrinsic tangential mechanics, not a deforming cell boundary.
candidates.feasibility: Lowest-cost 1D mechanochemical ring baseline; a physical curved-loop normal force balance would be an additional model.
candidates.use: Useful complementary fixed-ring model and analytical check. It cannot supply the missing Rac-dependent protrusive arm by itself.

additional_primary_sources.label: Dirks et al. (2019): Ezrin transport on a closed fixed cell
additional_primary_sources.title: A mathematical model for cell polarization in zebrafish primordial germ cells
additional_primary_sources.status: Author preprint; journal publication not verified
additional_primary_sources.assessment: Direct MCA relevance: membrane-bound Ezrin exchanges with cytoplasmic Ezrin, with closed-boundary transport and Darcy flow. However, the cell is deliberately static before bleb formation and the actin-brush body force is prescribed near a selected front. Its reduced simulation fixes the cytoplasmic concentration. This is a linker-transport insight rather than autonomous mechanical polarity closure.

bounded_addenda_20261019.label: Staddon, Munro and Banerjee (2022)
bounded_addenda_20261019.title: Pulsatile contractions and pattern formation in excitable actomyosin cortex
bounded_addenda_20261019.facts: Periodic one-dimensional porous Maxwell cortex coupled to cytosol; both RhoA and actomyosin are advected. The model explicitly imposes zero mixture flux. It has no separate membrane/MCA layer or normal shape dynamics.
bounded_addenda_20261019.inference: Continuity alone on a periodic domain permits a spatially constant circulating mixture flux; setting that flux to zero is an additional convention or physical restriction, not a consequence of periodicity.

bounded_addenda_20261019.label: Manakova, Yan, Lowengrub and Allard (2016)
bounded_addenda_20261019.title: Cell Surface Mechanochemistry and the Determinants of Bleb Formation, Healing, and Travel Velocity
bounded_addenda_20261019.facts: Local membrane/cortex-height mechanics combines force-sensitive MCA, cortex turnover, normal pressure and contractility. It produces bleb growth, healing and travel.
bounded_addenda_20261019.inference: Useful normal-MCA mechanism, but a global closed contour and free circulation were not verified. Nonuniform tension is discussed as a possible extension, so it is not credited here as an implemented closure.
